title.value: Beyond Mahalanobis-Based Scores for Textual OOD Detection
title.justification: The paper focuses on introducing a novel OOD detection method that goes beyond traditional Mahalanobis-based scores for detecting out-of-distribution samples in natural language processing tasks.
title.quote: In this paper, we introduce TRUSTED, a new OOD detector for classifiers based on Transformer architectures that meets operational requirements.

extractions.description: The paper presents TRUSTED, a novel out-of-distribution (OOD) detection method for classifiers based on Transformer architectures in Natural Language Processing (NLP). It addresses the limitations of current Mahalanobis distance-based methods, using the full breadth of information contained in the model's hidden layers. TRUSTED applies a similarity score based on data depth to detect OOD samples, providing significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior efficacy across multiple configurations, prompting a re-evaluation of checkpoint and seed impacts in OOD detection frameworks.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of this paper is about improving OOD detection in natural language processing, which, while valuable for AI safety and reliability, does not directly address climate or ecological sustainable development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This paper is about a critical safety issue, namely Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) detection [11], which refers to a change of distribution of incoming data that may cause failures of in-production AI systems.
